newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei hit by banking fears, tone fragile.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei hit by banking fears, tone fragile.

text.p: Fresh anxieties about Japan's financial sector triggered a sell-off in SIMEX Nikkei futures on Monday as the Nikkei share average ended two percent lower in Tokyo, dragged down by weakness in banking stocks.
Dealers said vague rumours that a Japanese bank had posted major losses in derivatives trading weighed on the market for much of the day.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract finished 325 points lower at 17,335 after hitting a low of 17,250.
News that Moody's Investors Service had lowered its ratings outlook for four Japanese banks to negative from stable further depressed sentiment, dealers said.
One trader said the Moody's news triggered fresh sales but added that the market could be in for a brief bounce on Tuesday on the perception that the downgrading was more severe than warranted.
"There was some short-covering towards the end of the day. I think this market's going to be bearish in the long-term but we might see a bit of a corrective bounce tomorrow," he said.
"There's decent support around 17,150-17,250 but if that goes, it'll go below 17,000 in a hurry," he added.
But a chartist with a local institution said a close below the 17,500 level sent a sell signal, exposing the market to further weakness.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract settled 1.2 points lower at 307.7 on a turnover of 103 lots.
